advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the acli tarball's top-level dir contains only the `acli` binary, or extract to a private dir and copy just `acli` into /usr/local/bin to avoid polluting PATH.
evidence: Dockerfile: `&& tar xzf /root/acli.tar.gz -C /usr/local/bin --strip-components=1 \`
CI extracts into an isolated dir: external-integration.yml:331 `tar xzf ~/.acli/acli.tar.gz -C ~/.acli/ --strip-components=1`
The build-time `acli --version` confirms the binary works but does not detect extra files landing on PATH.
advisory.finding: The acli tarball is extracted with `tar ... -C /usr/local/bin --strip-components=1`, which unpacks every top-level entry of the tarball (not just the `acli` binary) directly into /usr/local/bin. CI instead extracts into a private `~/.acli/` directory. If the tarball's top-level directory contains sibling files (LICENSE, README, completion scripts), they will pollute /usr/local/bin.
scenarios: The acli tarball ships a top-level dir containing more than just the binary.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Have the manifest test assert the AMD64 and ARM64 acli sha256 values are distinct (e.g. `len(set(shas)) >= 2`).
evidence: `shas = re.findall(r"ACLI_SHA256_(?:AMD64|ARM64)=([0-9a-fA-F]{64})", text)`
`assert len(shas) >= 2, f"expected a pinned sha256 per arch, found {shas!r}"`
The two arch digests must differ (amd64: f29fa8..., arm64: 72972e...) but the test never checks distinctness.
advisory.finding: The manifest test asserts `len(shas) >= 2` per-arch checksums exist but never asserts the AMD64 and ARM64 shas are distinct. A copy-paste error setting both ARGs to the same digest would pass the test yet fail the sha256sum verification for one architecture at build time.
scenarios: A future bump copies one arch's digest into both ARGs.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the assertion to also require distinct values, e.g. `assert len(set(shas)) >= 2`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Single-source the acli version+sha256 pin (or add a test asserting Dockerfile.mcp's ACLI_VERSION/ACLI_SHA256_* match CI's `vars.ACLI_VERSION`/`ACLI_SHA256` and docs/jira-sync-setup.md).
evidence: infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:46 `ARG ACLI_VERSION=1.3.19-stable`
external-integration.yml:316-317 `ACLI_VERSION: ${{ vars.ACLI_VERSION }}` / `ACLI_SHA256: ${{ vars.ACLI_SHA256 }}`
New test only checks existence, not parity: test_mcp_on_box_infra.py:157 `assert version and version != "latest"` and :166 `assert len(shas) >= 2` — never asserts the value matches CI/docs.

Contrast the existing byte-for-byte parity oracle for the Bedrock ids: docker-compose.yml:201-204 comment 'pinned byte-for-byte to .github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml by tests/unit/test_reviewbot_bedrock_cutover.py'.
infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:48 `ARG ACLI_SHA256_ARM64=72972e74...`
CI only ever fetches/verifies amd64: external-integration.yml:325 `..._linux_amd64.tar.gz`, :706, :852; reconcile-bridge.yml:201 `..._linux_amd64.tar.gz`
Dockerfile comment acknowledges the box is arm64: infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:43 'this image runs on the AL2023 **arm64** box ... while CI is amd64'
advisory.finding: The acli version and per-arch sha256 are hardcoded as ARG defaults in Dockerfile.mcp (ACLI_VERSION=1.3.19-stable + ACLI_SHA256_AMD64/ARM64), duplicating CI's `vars.ACLI_VERSION`/`vars.ACLI_SHA256` repo-variable pins with no oracle asserting parity — so the box image's acli pin can silently drift from CI's.
merged_from: The ACLI_SHA256_ARM64 pin — the arch that actually runs on the AL2023 arm64 box — has no CI coverage; every CI acli download/verify step targets only linux_amd64, so a wrong arm64 digest first fails at box build/deploy time rather than in CI.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extract the acli tarball into a scratch dir and install only the acli binary onto /usr/local/bin (mirror CI's isolated ~/.acli extraction) rather than untarring straight into a system PATH dir.
evidence: infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:62 `&& tar xzf /root/acli.tar.gz -C /usr/local/bin --strip-components=1 \`
infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:64 `&& chmod +x /usr/local/bin/acli \` (chmods only the one file)
CI extracts into an isolated dir: external-integration.yml:331 `tar xzf ~/.acli/acli.tar.gz -C ~/.acli/ --strip-components=1`
advisory.finding: The acli tarball is extracted directly into the shared PATH directory /usr/local/bin (`tar ... -C /usr/local/bin --strip-components=1`); CI instead extracts into a dedicated ~/.acli/ dir, so any non-binary members of the archive (license/readme) would be dumped into /usr/local/bin and only the `acli` file is chmod'd.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure Dockerfile.mcp ACLI_VERSION/ACLI_SHA256 pins share a single source of truth with CI's repo variables (or add a check that fails when they diverge).
evidence: ARG ACLI_VERSION=1.3.19-stable

Commit message: 'Provisioned exactly the way CI pins it (.github/workflows/external-integration.yml, the ACLI_VERSION/ACLI_SHA256 repo variables)' — but the Dockerfile embeds its own literal defaults rather than sourcing the CI-pinned values, so there is no single source of truth.
ABSENCE: no committed provenance/attestation linking these digests to a published Atlassian checksum or signature; the test only asserts the digests are 64 hex chars, not that they match upstream.
curl -sSL "https://acli.atlassian.com/linux/${ACLI_VERSION}/acli_${ACLI_VERSION}_linux_${acli_arch}.tar.gz"
ABSENCE: no LICENSE/notice or acknowledgement that acli is Atlassian-proprietary and being embedded in a distributed container image.
advisory.finding: The Dockerfile hardcodes ACLI_VERSION and per-arch ACLI_SHA256 defaults as ARG values that duplicate CI's ACLI_VERSION/ACLI_SHA256 repo variables, so the two independent pin sources can silently drift out of sync (image pins one version, CI validates another).
merged_from: The per-arch acli sha256 checksums are asserted by the author but there is no in-repo provenance record (e.g. a checksums file or upstream signature reference) tying f29fa8b7... / 72972e74... to the official Atlassian release, so the pin's correctness cannot be independently verified or re-validated.
The vendored `acli` binary (Atlassian CLI, proprietary EULA) is now baked into the shipped image, but no license posture / redistribution note is recorded for this new bundled third-party dependency.
scenarios: CI bumps ACLI_VERSION/ACLI_SHA256 repo variables but the Dockerfile ARG defaults are not updated (or vice versa), producing an image whose acli differs from the version validated in CI.
